reason: The name match is confirmed. The cited AUS page (opened) states "First place went to team Hayyakum, comprising Mahmoud Darwish, Amr Mohi Aldeen, Mohamad Dabbagh and Afif Zughayer" for the 1-2 November 2025 edition, and the independent sharjah24.ae report of 6 November 2025 (opened) carries the identical sentence. The 2026 mentor list is not published anywhere online: the official 2026 page auscse.com/hackathon (opened, 10-11 October 2026, AUS Main Building) names no mentors, and no search surfaced any 2026 mentor announcement. The only source for the 2026 mentor roster is the organizer's Mentor Profiles deck as recorded in D:\Sharjah Tourism Hackathon\00_Hackathon_Brief.md (lines 78 and 83: "Afif Zughayer | Founder, Amana Vision" and "Mahmoud Darwish | Founder, ReteIntel"), so the 2026 half rests on a private organizer document, not a web source. Supporting evidence that these are the same people: the AUS Spring 2026 Commencement list (ug_cen_spring_2026.pdf, opened and text-extracted) lists "Afif Ahmed Zughayer" and "Mahmoud Hany Darwish" as College of Engineering bachelor's candidates for 21 June 2026, consistent with 2025 student winners returning as alumni mentors in October 2026. One part of the claim is imprecise: ReteIntel is verifiable online. reteintel.com (opened) describes ReteIntel (FZE), based at SRTIP in Sharjah, an AI sensing, metering and control platform for buildings, energy and industry, and Masdar's Youth 4 Sustainability Out-of-Labs announcement of 21 January 2026 (opened) lists ReteIntel as "an AI-driven smart building platform that optimizes HVAC performance, predicts maintenance, and improves energy efficiency". Search snippets of Mahmoud Darwish's LinkedIn posts (profile itself blocked by LinkedIn authwall, HTTP 999) say he exhibited at Out-of-Labs during ADSW 2026 with Hayyakum teammate Amr Mohi Aldeen on an AI HVAC retrofit project, which matches ReteIntel's description. What remains unverified online is only the explicit "founder" attribution, since neither reteintel.com nor the Masdar page names any person. Amana Vision produced no online trace in four searches, so that part of the claim stands. Minor precision notes: the gap is about eleven months (1-2 November 2025 to 10-11 October 2026), and the 2025 edition was run by SCTDA with the AUS CSE department, while the 2026 edition is organized by AUS CSE and the School of Business Administration with SCTDA as ecosystem partner.
corrected_claim: Two mentors listed in the organizer's 2026 Mentor Profiles deck (recorded in the project brief), Mahmoud Darwish (Founder, ReteIntel) and Afif Zughayer (Founder, Amana Vision), share exact names with two members of Hayyakum, the first-place team of the 1-2 November 2025 Sharjah Tourism Innovation Hackathon at AUS (https://www.aus.edu/media/news/sharjah-tourism-innovation-hackathon-at-aus-reimagines-travel-and-tourism-experience; independently https://sharjah24.ae/en/Articles/2025/11/06/Innovation-Hackathon-reimagines-tourism-experience-at-AUS). No public 2026 mentor list exists online (https://auscse.com/hackathon/ names none). Both names also appear in the AUS Spring 2026 Commencement list of College of Engineering bachelor's candidates as "Afif Ahmed Zughayer" and "Mahmoud Hany Darwish" (https://www.aus.edu/sites/default/files/ug_cen_spring_2026.pdf), consistent with 2025 student winners returning as alumni mentors about eleven months later. ReteIntel is verifiable online: ReteIntel (FZE) is a Sharjah SRTIP-based AI building-control platform (https://reteintel.com/) exhibited at Masdar's Youth 4 Sustainability Out-of-Labs showcase at ADSW 2026 (https://masdar.ae/en/news/newsroom/youth-4-sustainability-announces-out-of-labs-winner-at-abu-dhabi-sustainability-week-2026), and search snippets of Darwish's LinkedIn posts describe him exhibiting there with Hayyakum teammate Amr Mohi Aldeen on an AI HVAC project; only the explicit founder attribution is not published. Amana Vision could not be found online.
